sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: L1: surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG immunofluorescence in 293T cells (receptor reaches plasma membrane). L5: N-terminally tagged full-length NMUR1 formed a stable complex with Gq and NMU peptide suitable for cryo-EM structure determination, demonstrating preserved ligand binding and G-protein coupling.
sites.rationale: NMUR1 has no signal peptide; residues 1–59 are extracellular per the topology landmarks, making the N-terminus the only extracellular terminus available for a tag. L1 explicitly states that the first 16 residues of NMUR1 were replaced by a prolactin SP + FLAG, pinning the junction: after SP cleavage the FLAG tag precedes native residue 17 (P), which is equivalent to an N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue = 0) in canonical numbering. Python confirms residue 1 = M and residue 17 = P; the tag is ≥44 residues from TM1 (starts at residue 60). L5 independently confirms the same N-terminal position with a larger fusion on full-length NMUR1 used in a functional cryo-EM study, elevating the validation to surface_and_function. Full-length NMUR1 expressed in 293T cells with the first 16 native residues replaced by a prolactin signal peptide (MNIKGSPWKGSLLLLLLVSNLLLCQSVAP) followed by a FLAG epitope tag; after SP cleavage the FLAG tag is displayed at the extracellular N-terminus. A second independent construct (L5, PMC9019041) fused BRIL + FLAG + 10×His N-terminally to full-length human NMUR1 and was used to determine the cryo-EM structure of the NMUR1–Gq–NMU complex, confirming surface trafficking, ligand binding, and G-protein coupling.

sources.claim: To construct the N-terminal tagged receptors, the first 16 amino acids of NMUR1 and the first 18 amino acids of NMUR2 or NMUR2S were substituted by a prolactin signal peptide (MNIKGSPWKGSLLLLLLVSNLLLCQSVAP) followed by an indicated epitope tag.

literature_notes: L2, L3, and L4 describe N-terminal and C-terminal FLAG tags on NMUR2 and NMUR2S (not NMUR1). NMUR2S has an extracellular C-terminus (unique short isoform), but NMUR1's C-terminus is intracellular (residues 360–426 per topology landmarks), so these lines do not support a C-terminal surface site on NMUR1. L6 (C-terminal LgBiT on NMUR1) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an internal loop insertion on NMUR1 or a close ortholog; ECL1 (119–135), ECL2 (200–229), and ECL3 (324–336) are not grounded by any ledger evidence and are therefore not proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT was inserted at the C-terminus of full-length human NMUR1 by homologous recombination; the C-terminus falls within the intracellular span 360–426 per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface site.
